title: Fulbright-Fogarty Public Health Fellowship Award (Jamaica)
description: A Fulbright research fellowship placement in Jamaica, offered through a partnership between the U.S. Department of State's Fulbright Program and the Fogarty International Center of the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), aimed at expanding research in public health and clinical research in resource-limited settings. Applicants select 'Public Health' as their field of study and must secure a letter of support from a site contact in Jamaica before applying, along with a CV and a concise (under 500 words) statement of research interest. There is a strong preference for applicants who do not hold dual US-Jamaican citizenship, though dual citizens may apply with strong justification. Like other Fulbright US Student grants, the award includes a stipend based on the host country's cost of living (covering housing, meals, and incidental costs), round-trip international travel, and accident/sickness health benefits for the grant period; the exact stipend amount is set annually and not published on the general award page. Open to US citizens currently enrolled in graduate or medical school (holding at least a bachelor's degree, not yet holding a PhD) at any US university. This is the 2027-2028 competition cycle.
org: U.S. Department of State (Fulbright Program) / NIH Fogarty International Center
visaNote: This is a funded research fellowship, not employment; visa/entry arrangements for Jamaica are coordinated as part of the Fulbright grant.
